fields.features_heading: What Emergent Puts Behind Each Yes or No
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the part a plain question list leaves out: what each answer does once it arrives.
fields.feature_1:
Questions drafted from one prompt

Describe the decision the survey feeds, and Emergent drafts each question with Yes and No as the answers. A follow-up prompt adds Maybe to one question or rewords another.
fields.feature_2:
A second question on the answer you pick

Choose which answer opens a follow-up. A No can ask what went wrong while a Yes moves straight on, so a satisfied customer answers a single question and is done with it.
fields.feature_3:
Each answer saved as a row you own

Every answer lands in a database you own, with the date and a group you tag, such as plan or class section. Count the Yes answers for one group without a spreadsheet.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts on the answers that need a person

Set a rule on any answer, and the person who owns it hears by Slack or email. Reminders go to anyone who has not answered by the deadline, and they stop once they do.
fields.feature_5:
One question per screen on a phone

People answer on a phone one question at a time, tapping Yes or No and moving on. There is no cap on the number of responses, so it can go to every customer you have.
fields.feature_6:
Your own domain and your own code

Run the survey on your own domain, included in Emergent and billed in credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository, with every question and rule.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Teams Act on a Yes or No
fields.tab_content_1:
Every No reaches the support lead in Slack

Quillfeather Home Goods closes a support ticket and asks the customer one question: was your issue resolved? In one week, 340 customers answered and 51 said No. Each No opened a follow-up asking what still was not working, and the support lead got a Slack alert with the ticket number.
fields.tab_content_2:
31 students said No, and 22 pointed at step 4

After every lab, a Birchgrove High chemistry teacher asks 84 students one question: could you follow the steps without help? This time 78 answered and 31 said No. The follow-up asked which step lost them, and 22 of the 31 named step 4. The teacher rewrote step 4 before the next lab.
fields.tab_content_3:
Saturday pickup opens when Yes reaches 40

Fallowfield Farm wants to know whether its 150 share members would collect their boxes on Saturday morning. The question offers Yes, No, and Maybe. Of the 96 members who answered, 44 said Yes, 21 said Maybe, and 31 said No. With Yes past the farm's threshold of 40, the Saturday slot opened.
fields.tab_content_4:
64 of 90 early risers said No to a 7 a.m. opening

Cordova Hill Fitness counts its early risers before it changes hours. It asked 600 members whether they would stay if the gym opened at 7 a.m. instead of 5 a.m., and 212 answered. Among early risers who check in before 7, 64 of 90 said No. Among the other 122 members, 18 said No. The owner kept the 5 a.m. opening.

fields.howto_title: How to Write a Yes or No Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a yes no questions survey where every answer is easy to read and leads to an action.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Name the decision each answer feeds
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask about one thing per question
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Offer Maybe only for the future
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the decision the survey informs, such as whether to open a Saturday pickup. Keep only the questions whose Yes or No would change that decision. Put the decision in your prompt, and Emergent drafts the questions around it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Split any question with "and" in it. "Was the agent quick and helpful?" gets a No you cannot read, because the customer may mean either half. Ask "Was the agent quick?" and "Was the agent helpful?" as two separate questions.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Pew Research Center reports that less educated and less informed respondents have a greater tendency to agree with agree-disagree statements. Ask about events instead: "Did your order arrive on the promised date?" rather than "Do you agree delivery was fast?"
fields.howto_step_4_des: Add Maybe where an honest person may not know the answer yet, like a plan for next month. Leave it off questions about the past: people know whether their order arrived, and Maybe gives them a way to skip the question.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Choose what a No sets off
fields.howto_step_5_des: Pick the answer that needs a person and say what happens after it: a follow-up question, an alert to the person who owns the problem, or both. Write that rule into your prompt, and Emergent builds it into the survey.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Tag each answer with a group
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide before launch which groups you will compare, like plan or class section, and tag every answer with one. A split by group shows who said No, which one total for the whole survey hides.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test both paths, then read the counts
fields.howto_step_7_des: Answer the survey yourself twice, once Yes and once No, and check that each path does what you set. After launch, read the No count beside the number of people asked, not only beside the number who answered.

faq_plan.q: What are some good yes or no survey questions?
faq_plan.ref: What are some good yes or no survey questions?

prov.original: What are some good yes or no survey questions?

faq_plan.a: Good yes or no survey questions ask about one thing the person knows for certain, such as "Did your order arrive on time?" or "Have you used the new booking page?" Each has one honest answer. A No points at something you can fix, and a follow-up can ask what went wrong.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a yes no questions survey?
faq_plan.a: Describe the decision you need to make to Emergent's AI survey builder, and it drafts the questions and the table that stores every answer. Add a follow-up on No or an alert with a second prompt, then share the survey link.

faq_plan.q: When should yes no maybe survey questions include Maybe?
faq_plan.a: Include Maybe when people are deciding something that has not happened yet, like attending next month. Report Maybe as its own count, never split between Yes and No, and give each Maybe one follow-up asking what would make it a Yes. If Maybe beats Yes, ask again closer to the date.

faq_plan.q: What are survey questions answerable by yes or no called?
faq_plan.ref: survey questions answerable by yes or no
faq_plan.a: They are closed-ended questions, where people are asked to choose from a list of answer choices, in Pew Research Center's words. With two choices they are also called dichotomous: a question which can have two possible answers. In a customer experience survey, add one open question for the reason behind each No.

faq_plan.q: Should survey questions offer yes, no, and somewhat?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the honest answer is a matter of degree, such as whether a guide was useful. Leave Somewhat off questions of fact, because an order either arrived or it did not. Count Somewhat on its own line, and if it wins, rewrite the question as a rating on a 5-point scale.

faq_plan.q: What are some examples of yes or no survey questions for work?
faq_plan.ref: yes or no survey questions examples
faq_plan.a: Ask employees "Do you have the tools you need?" or "Did you take a full lunch break?" Ask event guests "Would you attend again next year?" On Emergent, each question can open its own follow-up when someone answers No.

faq_plan.q: What are good yes or no customer service survey questions?
faq_plan.ref: yes or no customer service survey questions
faq_plan.a: Ask about the contact that just ended: "Was your issue resolved?" and "Did you have to explain the problem more than once?" Send 2 or 3 questions right after the ticket closes. For price, product range, or delivery, a longer customer feedback survey is the better fit.

faq_plan.q: Which survey questions for students work as yes or no?
faq_plan.ref: survey questions for students yes or no
faq_plan.a: Ask about one lesson or task, like "Did you finish the reading?" or "Could you hear the speaker?" Match the wording to the students' reading level. Leave out anything that asks a student to judge a classmate.

faq_plan.q: What is the best way of analyzing yes no survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Count the Yes and No answers for each question, divide by the number who answered, and report the share beside the count, such as 18 No out of 120. Then split the counts by group, because one overall share can hide a group that said No far more. Check the number who answered against the number asked before you trust a share.

faq_plan.q: How many survey questions with yes or no answers should one survey have?
faq_plan.ref: survey questions with yes or no answers
faq_plan.a: Keep it under 10, and close with one open question so people can say what the Yes and No answers missed. A first-week onboarding survey, for example, can ask 6 yes or no questions and end with that open one. With no cap on responses in Emergent, the same survey can go to every new hire each month.

plan.angle: The top 10 is question lists and templates (SurveyMonkey, Typeform, survey blogs) plus a scoring thread; none shows what a yes or no answer triggers once it lands. This page shows four yes no surveys built from a prompt, each with the follow-up or rule a single answer sets off: a support check that alerts the lead on every No, a lab check that finds the step students could not follow, a Yes, No, or Maybe vote with a threshold, and a split by member group that changes a decision. The FAQ gives wording advice, examples by audience, and how to read the counts.
